stop_status: REPAIRED - the STOP-level NEO-ERR-1 external-ABI defect is fixed: openssl_rs_err_take_data now always returns NULL or a crate-owned seam block, copying borrowed slot data before the C variadic adapter can realloc it. The negative control fires on the pre-fix shape. Nothing is promoted to SAFETY_DISCHARGED or SAFE_COMPATIBLE; the full ERR mechanism remains CONTRACTED because NEO-ERR-3/4/6/7 are contract-only and independently unchecked.

authority.abi: C ABI unchanged: no exported symbol, signature, #[repr(C)] layout or CRYPTO_* seam coordinate changed. The private Rust->C helper signatures were deliberately kept; the change is inside openssl_rs_err_take_data's ownership contract.
external_contracts: ERR_set_error_data(data, flags): data is NULL or NUL-terminated within a readable allocation; without ERR_TXT_MALLOCED the queue borrows and never releases it; with the flag the caller transfers one whole seam block exclusively.
ERR_vset_error reuses the slot's detached data buffer; the adapter reallocs it unconditionally. B33 makes that sound by keeping the detach point always owned.
OSSL_ERR_STATE_save/save_to_mark clear (and therefore release) the destination, so every MALLOCED slot in the destination must already be an exclusively owned seam block.
OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore trusts err_data_size as the source extent and duplicates err_file/err_func as NUL-terminated strings; the source state must not be mutated concurrently.
ERR_error_string(e, NULL) aliases a process-global 256-byte buffer; callers must serialize calls and reads externally.
CRYPTO_malloc-family `file` is NULL or a NUL-terminated debug string read on failure.
An allocator hook installed by CRYPTO_set_mem_functions must not re-enter ERR on the same thread while ERR holds &mut on its state.

boundaries.operation: openssl_rs_err_take_data ownership transfer to the C variadic adapter
boundaries.before: Detached es->err_data[top] and returned it regardless of ERR_TXT_MALLOCED; err_variadic.c:140/153 then CRYPTO_realloc'd it. A borrowed pointer could reach the allocator.
boundaries.after: Detaches in all cases; MALLOCED transfers the block, borrowed is copied into slot_buf_alloc(err_data_size) and the original is untouched; NULL/zero-extent returns NULL. The slot is always cleared. # Safety/ownership text and the adapter comment record the invariant.
boundaries.mechanism: ELIMINATED (the borrowed pointer can no longer reach CRYPTO_realloc); ownership now encodes 'always a seam block' at the detach point.

boundaries.before: Stored an arbitrary size; OSSL_ERR_STATE_restore later copies that many bytes.
boundaries.after: # Safety states size >= 1, size <= allocation extent and a NUL within size. A zero-extent MALLOCED block is released through the seam and not stored.
boundaries.mechanism: CONTRACTED + partial enforcement; an overstated non-zero size remains a caller obligation.
boundaries.state: FIXED (contract + zero-extent check; not independently checked)

boundaries.before: Destination clear releases MALLOCED slots with no documented ownership/provenance requirement.
boundaries.after: Both # Safety blocks now require OSSL_ERR_STATE_new provenance (or every MALLOCED slot to satisfy the slot contract), exclusive ownership and no concurrent mutation.
boundaries.mechanism: RELOCATED to an external contract; no ABI-compatible runtime provenance marker exists.

boundaries.before: # Safety said only 'live state owned by the caller'.
boundaries.after: States err_data readable for exactly err_data_size bytes, err_file/err_func NULL or NUL-terminated until return, and no concurrent mutation; ties the extent to NEO-ERR-2.

boundaries.before: Prose noted the authority's shared static; # Safety did not require external synchronization.
boundaries.after: # Safety states the process-global alias, mandatory external serialization and valid-until-next-call lifetime. The shared static is retained for authority-compatible pointer identity/overwrite behaviour; no divergence.

boundaries.before: The failure/overflow path reads `file` as a C string; the safe entry points did not state the precondition.
boundaries.after: All four document NULL-or-NUL-terminated `file` valid for the call and explicitly deny that the raw pointer is a safe Rust value.
boundaries.mechanism: RETAINED: documentation does not make a safe fn sound for an arbitrary raw pointer.

boundaries.before: The non-reentrancy rule existed only in err.rs; CRYPTO_set_mem_functions' # Safety did not state it.
boundaries.after: CRYPTO_set_mem_functions # Safety now states the rule (same-thread ERR re-entry forbidden; allocation/release and other-thread re-entry allowed). The guard is not implemented.
boundaries.mechanism: RELOCATED to the external installer contract.
